name: Cloak and Dagger, Entwined
oracle_text:
Deathtouch, lifelink
When Cloak and Dagger enter, choose target opponent and up to one target creature they control. They reveal their hand. You may exile a nonland card from their hand or the chosen creature until Cloak and Dagger leave the battlefield.
blocked_sentences: When Cloak and Dagger enter, choose target opponent and up to one target creature they control.
You may exile a nonland card from their hand or the chosen creature until Cloak and Dagger leave the battlefield.

needs.what: an exile-until-this-permanent-leaves link that returns each exiled card to the zone it came from -- the nonland card exiled out of a hand goes back to its owner's hand, the creature exiled off the battlefield goes back to the battlefield -- from a single return, since one printed sentence covers both
needs.why_existing_wont_do: exile's 'until_leaves' only records the link; the return is an ordinary leaves_battlefield trigger whose op hardwires one destination (Oblivion Ring uses put_onto_battlefield over {'zone':'exile','exiled_with':'self'}, return_to_hand always moves to Zone.HAND). Nothing on the exiled object records the zone it was exiled from, so no condition or selector can split the returned cards by origin, and picking either op would send half the cases to the wrong zone

needs.what: one optional 'you may' choice, made on resolution, that picks a single object from either of two disjoint pools -- a nonland card in the revealed hand, or the creature this ability targeted -- and offers the creature half only when the optional target was actually chosen
needs.why_existing_wont_do: 'may' wraps a single fixed effect, and a 'choose_mode' of two exile effects is announced as a mode list whose entries do not know whether the 'up to one target creature' was taken: with no creature targeted, the second mode would still be offered and its exile would resolve over an empty target list, doing nothing while reading as a choice. Two 'may'-wrapped exiles in sequence is also wrong -- it lets the controller exile a hand card AND the creature, where the printed card exiles exactly one
